scenarios.title: Explicit shadow profile resolves once or refuses before transport

gherkin.given: the committed policy declares the two approved shadow profiles and their required runtime bindings
gherkin.when: an operator selects one profile for a frozen author request
gherkin.then: exactly that profile and model are frozen, while missing or unknown selection and invalid bindings refuse before any HTTP request

obligations.requiredProof: Production-unit assertions validate both committed profile records, exact provider and model identity, and deterministic one-profile resolution.
Named negative-path assertions prove missing, unknown, and incomplete profile selection refuses before the loopback server receives any request.
The production shadow CLI executes only the explicitly selected profile and consumes its required runtime endpoint and model bindings.

scenarios.title: One bounded transport qualifies the exact model and returns a schema-constrained JSON object

gherkin.given: an explicitly selected profile has a valid runtime endpoint and exact configured model
gherkin.when: the shadow runtime performs preflight and authors the frozen request
gherkin.then: it confirms the model through /v1/models before one bounded /v1/chat/completions call and returns the exact contractVersion and requestFingerprint with the request-specific brief or final object value, a stop finish reason, downstream strict validation, and a truthful normalized usage state whose measured token values and computed sum are non-negative safe integers without synthesized missing values

obligations.requiredProof: Provider-free production-normalizer assertions reject unsafe prompt, completion, and total token values; reject addition overflow before computing a sum; and preserve missing or null values as unmeasured without synthesizing zero or a total.

Actual OMLX and Ollama endpoint checks observe exact model discovery followed by one schema-fixed three-key response envelope with an object payload, stop finish reason, and downstream strict validation.
Each provider canary reaches the explicitly configured external endpoint and validates model discovery, candidate JSON, and measured-or-unmeasured usage without fixture substitution.
A stress assertion exercises every declared byte, deadline, retry, and in-flight limit at its exact cap and at cap plus one.
Both real provider checks execute the model and endpoint supplied by the selected profile's committed binding names and runtime environment.

scenarios.title: Shadow authorship remains non-authoritative and powerless

gherkin.given: the current Copilot worker, scheduler, public payload, pointer, history, and Git state are authoritative
gherkin.when: the shadow CLI processes a frozen author request under either approved profile
gherkin.then: the canonical request fingerprint is verified before any process, transport, or HTTP dispatch, and the invocation writes nothing, exposes no secret-shaped value, offers no production action, and leaves every authoritative surface byte-identical

obligations.requiredProof: The exported verifier reuses the canonical author-request projection and rejects each retained-digest mutation across contractVersion, data, provider, model, promptPolicy, schema, validator, and maxOutputTokens.
Publication-shaped options and unsafe or secret-shaped values produce named refusals with no tracked artifact or Git mutation.
Dispatch counters prove every retained-digest mutation refuses before an invokeAuthor callback or child spawn, before route dispatch, and before adapter model preflight or HTTP work.
A production shadow CLI invocation exercises the selected profile while snapshots prove production state does not change.

Static owner, consumer, and deployment-inventory assertions prove the protected production files are unchanged, have no shadow import, retain the current payload validator, and declare rlbriefroute.js as Node/shadow-only with no public runtime consumer.
